_about: DISC-016 six-chapter redesign declared additions (founder approval, 4 Nov 2026): chapter labels, titles and standfirsts, the chapter 04 checklist (each line drawn from facts already on the page and linked to its detail), the 'Further afield' summary, and the chapter 06 decision (A and B). Every other text block is the production text, moved.
blocks: The possibility
A space above the ordinary garden.
A different perspective
The garden, seen from the canopy.
Lifted even a metre or two, the same garden looks different: you see over the hedge, into the branches, and back at the house. The ground stays where it was; what changes is where you stand.
More than a treehouse
One idea, many uses.
A den, a play structure, a quiet retreat, a games room or a studio. Not every structure suits every use, and none of them is somewhere to live.
What it can become
Making it possible
What decides whether it works.
Seven things to think through before anything is ordered, each with its detail on this page.
Trees and support
No tree is needed. A structure can stand on its own posts, share the load with a tree, or be carried by one.
Trees and support No tree is needed. A structure can stand on its own posts, share the load with a tree, or be carried by one. Three ways it can stand
Tree health

If a tree is involved, have an arborist look at it before anything is designed. On PlotNua’s reading of the professional guidance, the risk near a tree sits mostly in the footings and digging, inside the root protection area. A Tree Preservation Order may also apply.

Tree health If a tree is involved, have an arborist look at it before anything is designed. On PlotNua’s reading of the professional guidance, the risk near a tree sits mostly in the footings and digging, inside the root protection area. A Tree Preservation Order may also apply. Trees, safety and insurance
Access and safety
Steps, a ladder or a bridge, and the clear space around them, all take ground. EN 1176 does not cover private gardens, so ask a builder which standard, if any, they commit to.

Access and safety Steps, a ladder or a bridge, and the clear space around them, all take ground. EN 1176 does not cover private gardens, so ask a builder which standard, if any, they commit to. The practical questions
Garden size and location
Garden structures are counted together, nothing of this kind may go forward of the front wall, and private open space to the rear or side must not drop below 25 m².

Garden size and location Garden structures are counted together, nothing of this kind may go forward of the front wall, and private open space to the rear or side must not drop below 25 m². Space, and a future garden house
Planning
Height is the deciding number: usually 3 metres overall in the exemption considered here. Only a section 5 declaration gives a binding answer.
Planning Height is the deciding number: usually 3 metres overall in the exemption considered here. Only a section 5 declaration gives a binding answer. Why height matters
Neighbours
Overlooking is a design conversation. One published Dublin project sits in the canopy specifically to avoid looking into neighbouring gardens.
Neighbours Overlooking is a design conversation. One published Dublin project sits in the canopy specifically to avoid looking into neighbouring gardens. Will the neighbours see in?
Maintenance and weather
Ask who services it, how often and at what rate, and what the written structural warranty excludes. Irish makers typically roof these in felt, shingles or steel.
